description:
We're a team passionate about aerospace, engineering, and technology, with interests in software development, problem-solving, and innovative design. Our background includes hands-on engineering experience, technical projects, and previous participation in NASA Space Apps. We're excited to collaborate, explore new ideas, and develop a creative, technically sound solution to a real-world challenge.

Our team is already formed, so we're not currently looking for additional members.
summary:
Project Rocket League is a health monitoring app designed to help astronauts track their health during space missions. It brings important health data into one place, making it easier to monitor vital signs, spot potential health issues, and understand an astronaut's overall condition.

Our goal is to make health monitoring in space simpler, faster, and more accessible. Since astronauts have limited access to medical support, having a clear and easy-to-use system can help them make better decisions about their health.

The app features a simple dashboard that presents health information in an easy-to-understand format, helping astronauts and mission teams stay informed.
details:
Project Rocket League is a web-based health monitoring system designed for astronauts during space missions.

The app brings an astronaut's health information into one dashboard, allowing users to monitor vital signs, track changes over time, and identify potential health concerns.

The goal is to help astronauts understand their health and make informed decisions, especially during long-duration missions where immediate medical assistance may not be available.

Our team focused on making the app simple, accessible, and easy to navigate. We wanted important health information to be clearly displayed without overwhelming the user.

The project was developed as a web application, with a frontend for displaying and interacting with health data and a backend for processing and managing information.

We hope this project demonstrates how digital health monitoring tools could help improve astronaut safety and support future space exploration.
projectRefs: Why Do We Conduct Science Experiments in Space?
